methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter retrospective comparative cohort (MMF n=31 vs infliximab n=21) with well-described inclusion/exclusion criteria, CTCAE v5.0 grading, and a steroid-refractory definition. Strengths include center-stratified sensitivity analyses that detected a confound (all MMF patients from Heidelberg, where infliximab patients also had higher steroid exposure), Cox regression for steroid dose effects on PFS/OS, and consideration of CMV, C. difficile, and endoscopic confirmation. Key weaknesses: non-randomized allocation with center-driven treatment choice creates substantial confounding, small sample size limits statistical power (explicitly acknowledged), no propensity matching, retrospective chart review without standardized documentation, non-uniform ipilimumab regimens (10 mg/kg, 3 mg/kg, combos), and no adjustment for subsequent lines of ICI therapy in PFS/OS analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective comparative case series of 52 steroid-refractory ir colitis patients falls at Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case series). Clinical relevance is high because MMF offers an oral, low-cost, well-tolerated alternative in settings where infliximab is contraindicated or unavailable, addressing a real practice gap where irAE management guidelines mostly recommend infliximab. Findings are directly actionable for multidisciplinary irAE teams even if definitive comparative efficacy requires prospective data.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort study where STROBE applies. Baseline characteristics (Table 1), outcome definitions, statistical tests, censoring rules, and limitations section are reported; subgroup/center-comparison analyses are explicitly described. However, no STROBE checklist, no flow diagram of exclusions at each step, no formal sample size justification, and multiplicity corrections across subgroup tests are not mentioned. Data availability score is 2 because patient-level Tables S1/S2 are referenced but no repository or code is provided; data sharing is effectively on-request at best.

novelty_literature.justification: MMF has been described in ICI irAEs (hepatitis, some case reports of colitis) and one prospective study (Mir et al., ref 20) evaluated upfront MMF in ICI colitis. This paper's novel contributions are the focus on steroid-refractory patients (vs. upfront), a direct head-to-head comparison with infliximab, and the inclusion of oncological outcomes (PFS/OS) plus cumulative steroid exposure. This is a meaningful incremental extension in a niche but clinically important area.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with detailed methods, precise numerical reporting (medians, ranges, p-values), and thoughtful discussion that integrates contradictory literature on anti-TNF and steroid exposure effects. Figures and tables are described coherently and the center-effect sensitivity analysis is logically presented. Minor issues: some methodological details are scattered between methods and results, and the abstract is long.

key_strengths: Addresses a clinically important gap—alternative to infliximab in steroid-refractory ir colitis—with a 14-year multicenter cohort
Transparent center-stratified sensitivity analysis that identifies center rather than drug as the likely driver of steroid-exposure differences
Comprehensive outcome set including response, time to response, recurrence, CMV positivity, cumulative steroid dose, PFS, and OS
Explicit acknowledgment of retrospective-design limitations and non-uniform management
key_concerns: Non-randomized treatment allocation strongly confounded with center (all MMF cases from Heidelberg), limiting causal inference
Small sample sizes (31 vs 21) with tendency toward higher infliximab response rate (95.2% vs 77.4%, p=0.081) that may be underpowered rather than truly non-inferior
Heterogeneous ipilimumab regimens (10 mg/kg, 3 mg/kg, combinations with nivolumab or vemurafenib) not adjusted for in outcome analyses
No propensity score matching or formal comparative-effectiveness adjustment
Data availability is limited to referenced supplementary tables without repository or code sharing
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically relevant, honestly reported retrospective comparison with acknowledged limitations; suitable for a mid-tier specialty oncology journal after minor revisions to strengthen statistical handling of confounding and add a STROBE checklist.
